title: Lock Escalation: One Big Update Locks the Whole Table
description: A single huge UPDATE escalates to a table lock and blocks an unrelated row; batching it under the escalation threshold keeps locks fine-grained.
narrative:
## Scenario
A nightly job (Session A) posts interest to 40,000 ledger rows inside one transaction. Meanwhile Session B just wants to correct **one** unrelated row at the far end of the table. B hangs until the batch job commits — even though the two never touch the same rows.

## Why it blocks
SQL Server starts with fine-grained **row/page locks**, but once a single statement acquires roughly **5,000 locks** it trades them all for one coarse **table lock** — this is **lock escalation**. A's 40,000-row `UPDATE` sails past that threshold and takes an exclusive lock on the *entire* `Ledger` table. Now B's update of row 49,999 can't get even a single row lock, because the whole table is locked. B blocks for the full duration of A's transaction.

## What to look for
- A's `UPDATE` shows a table-level `X` lock (escalated), not thousands of row locks.
- B is blocked waiting on an **object-level** lock it should never have needed.

## The concept
Keep any one statement under the escalation threshold so it never grabs the table. **Batch** the work — update in chunks of ~2,000 rows, each committing on its own — so A only ever holds a handful of locks at a time and B's unrelated row stays free. (The blunt alternative is `ALTER TABLE Ledger SET (LOCK_ESCALATION = DISABLE)`, but batching also shortens how long any lock is held.)
startingQuery: -- This is a concurrency lesson. Rewrite Session A's giant UPDATE to run in batches, then Run the interleaving.
hints: B is blocked on a table-level lock, but it only wants one row. Something made A lock the whole table.
A single statement that locks ~5,000+ rows escalates to one table lock. A's UPDATE hits 40,000 rows in one shot.
Split A's UPDATE into batches under the threshold, each auto-committing: WHILE loop doing UPDATE ... WHERE LedgerId BETWEEN @i AND @i+1999; so it never escalates.

interleaving.description: Session A updates 40,000 rows in one transaction and escalates to a table lock; Session B's single-row update on an unrelated row blocks behind it.

A.sql: BEGIN TRAN; UPDATE Ledger SET Amount = Amount + 1 WHERE LedgerId <= 40000;

B.sql: UPDATE Ledger SET Amount = Amount + 5 WHERE LedgerId = 49999;

interleaving.solutionNote: Rewrite A's single 40,000-row UPDATE into a WHILE loop that updates ~2,000 rows per iteration and auto-commits each batch, so no statement ever reaches the ~5,000-lock escalation threshold. A then only holds a few locks at a time and B's unrelated row (49999) is never blocked. Alternatively ALTER TABLE Ledger SET (LOCK_ESCALATION = DISABLE).
